scientific_queries.note: Joint unseen cell and drug holdout on GDSC.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round establishes a transfer boundary and explicitly labels the strictest cell as underpowered rather than null.

design.holdout: 20% of 125 cells and 20% of 65 drugs jointly
design.training: seen cells x both-seen drugs only (about 54,256 keys, roughly 50% of the data)
pools: strict (unseen cell x both drugs unseen)

headline: ranking value holds whenever at least one side is seen (unseen cell +6.88 pp, unseen drug +5.00 pp, both +4.00 pp) but is not established when the cell and both drugs are simultaneously unseen (+1.18 pp, CI includes 0)
notable: the unseen-CELL pool shows the LARGEST gain of the four (+6.88 pp), so the cell side is not the bottleneck
power_caveat: the strict pool has only 449 keys (an order of magnitude smaller than the others), only 38 of 40 splits yielded data, and the CI upper bound is +2.76 pp; this is underpowered, not a demonstrated null
limits: the joint holdout shrinks training to about 50% of keys, so part of the drop is weaker training rather than novelty
tissue is still seen for held-out cells, so complete unfamiliarity is not achieved
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI

register_updates.C43: new, exploratory: transfer boundary along the joint-novelty axis

next_gates: raise power on the strict cell by widening it to 'unseen cell x at least one drug unseen' (already established at +4.00 pp) or by using cross-screen data, which is smaller still
